obligations.note: manage_payees is a privileged action, but POST /payees/{id}/reopen is registered with mfa=False and is served to any authorized caller. EXC-0185 only covers that path for the reconciliation batch account, and the handler does not enforce that limit. The exhaustive control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails on this route.
The new store update writes only status and closed_at. NPI columns stay sealed, and test_every_npi_field_is_sealed_at_rest passed on the head commit.
reopen_payee authorizes, updates the payee, then records an audit event with actor, action reopen_payee, target payee id, and the service clock. The sampled audit control test passed.
reopen_payee uses a fixed SQL string and binds the payee id as a parameter. The exhaustive SQL control test passed on the head commit.
The change names ticket CHG-25599, which change manager Erik Brandt approved on 2026-10-20 before review. Its components cover payments.http, payments.routes, payments.service, and payments.store.
Sofia Santos, a payments change approver and not the author, approved a code review of commit 37fd467431e0194b1e979e1663cfd3fe865214ec.
The code review and the security review both name the only commit on the change, which is the head commit.
CI run.json for commit 37fd467431e0194b1e979e1663cfd3fe865214ec reports failure. The registered MFA-1 control test is unskipped and failing, so the payments suite did not pass on the final commit.
app.py, routes.py, and store.py are security-sensitive. Ines Halvorsen, a security reviewer and not the author, approved a security review of the head commit.

EXC-0185 is approved, unexpired, and has a compensating control, but its scope is only the reconciliation batch account. The merged route skips MFA for every caller, so the exception does not authorize the deviation.
Acceptance record ACR-0404 covered routes.py for MFA-1, and this change alters that file's behavior, so that evidence lapses. The replacement exhaustive control test on the head commit failed.

summary: The change adds POST /payees/{id}/reopen for the privileged action manage_payees without MFA, while the matching close route requires MFA. EXC-0185 does not cover that behavior because it is limited to a reconciliation batch account and the code never checks the caller. CI on the head commit fails the exhaustive privileged-route control test, so testing evidence is not adequate and the prior MFA acceptance record for routes.py has lapsed. Encryption, audit, parameterized SQL, the ticket, and the independent code and security approvals are in order, but the MFA deviation is not acceptable.
